class_id: bumping a shared EXTRACTOR_VERSION constant to fix an extraction bug re-opens every COMPLETED document in the live window for re-read, and the re-read backlog queues ahead of genuinely new, never-read documents under the same spawn budget
feature: the document re-read scheduler (spawn budget order OPEN -> CLOSED -> UPCOMING) that decides, each cycle, which document gets the next extraction slot; any fix that bumps EXTRACTOR_VERSION to force existing COMPLETED documents to be re-extracted with corrected logic
symptom: a version bump is the only mechanism to get a corrected extractor to re-read documents it already extracted wrongly, but it has no separate lane: the re-opened backlog and brand-new incoming documents (a fresh RHP just filed) compete for the same per-cycle spawn budget, and the scheduler's own ordering (never-read-first was NOT the default before PR #1172 r1) let the backlog starve new arrivals. Measured 2026-09-27 (#771/#1247): the 2026-09-26 version bump (PR #1138) left 48 documents undrained 26 hours later; a second bump the same contract run (PR #1172, for the ratio-parsing fix) would have added roughly 97 more re-opens (33 of them price-band ads with no ratio to extract at all), on top of the still-undrained 48. Wider shape: any shared version-triggered mass re-open competes with the system's own no-backoff-timer, new-work-first design intent (ist-timezone/spec §2.5.1 analog for extraction) unless the scheduler explicitly protects new arrivals.
first_seen: 2026-09-26 to 2026-09-27, IPODhan, issues #771 and #1247 (contract 1): PROGRESS line 2026-09-27 21:16 IST measured the @09-26 bump (PR #1138) had 48 undrained documents 26 hours later, and projected the @09-27 bump (PR #1172, issuer_ratio_yield fix) would add ~97 more re-opens including 33 price-band ads with no ratio field at all.
fix_prs: #1172 r1 (2026-09-27): never-read documents are now scheduled first (two-pass budget split), and re-reads are scoped to only the affected extractor-version/document-type combination (22 re-opens instead of the naive ~97) rather than every COMPLETED document unconditionally. #1254 (#1247, 2026-09-28): a reserved re-read slot per cycle plus a spawn-once-per-IPO-per-cycle cap, cutting the drain time for the existing 143-document re-read backlog from ~14 days to ~8 days (later corrected: 143 candidates measured directly, not the earlier ~22 estimate).
detection_check: none dedicated at the scheduler level. The floor check issuer_ratio_yield (and the general document_fetch_state age checks, e.g. m_blocked_all_age) can show a document sitting unread for a long time, but nothing asserts 'a version-bump backlog drains within N days' or 'new documents are never starved behind a re-read backlog' as an explicit, alertable invariant.
